title: The qualifying cost is not a cost: NudgeRatchet._dispatch recycles 100% of it back into the pot, making the M-01 claim repeatable
severityNote: Medium. Confidence: high on the mechanism, medium that production wires both legs simultaneously. This is what makes M-01 repeatable rather than one-shot.
note:
[phoenix-nft-staking-25] NEW MEDIUM @5015f1b (DEDUP-25-02). batchMint steps 6+7 pay `price` to NFTMinterV2._executeMint, which safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, config.dispatcher, price); NudgeRatchet._dispatch (lib/mutable/yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol:83-101, transfer at :100) then does IERC20(_token).safeTransfer(batchMinter, bal) - 100% OF BALANCE, per its own NatSpec 'DESIGN: this sweeps the FULL token balance, not the `amount` argument.' Per §4.2 donate-forward, D arrives AFTER the snapshot, so it is not refunded to this batcher - it seeds the NEXT one. Steady state per claim cycle: searcher +P-C cash, +count NFTs, -gas; pot re-armed to exactly C; protocol USDC retained ZERO. The SECOND claim is a pure C -> C round-trip: the searcher recovers their entire qualifying cost and keeps nudgeSize NFTs for the price of gas alone. THE QUALIFYING COST STOPS BEING A COST.

This FALSIFIES KI #15's own load-bearing premise ('a bot that claims it must first pay more payment-token into the protocol than it extracts in reward; every claim is net-positive for the protocol') and therefore sits OUTSIDE KI #15 on a second independent ground beyond carve-out (d): an acceptance covers the risk AS IT STOOD; it cannot cover a risk whose stated bound does not exist.

NudgeStreamer does NOT close this - it is a TIMING THROTTLE, NOT A VALUE CAP (_accrued = min(rewardPerSecond * elapsed / PRECISION, buffer), NudgeStreamer.sol:192-199; concurs with this project's own run-24 note). A patient searcher recovers 100% of C after `duration`.

LAW-3 FRAMING (footgun, in scope): two ORDINARY owner settings compose - NudgeRatchet.batchMinter = <this contract> (its designed purpose) and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.dispatcherIndex = <the ratchet index> (blessed by docs §4.1). A competent, non-malicious owner would be SURPRISED that the batch minter paying its mints through the dispatcher that funds its own pot creates a closed loop. No malicious-owner vector is asserted. CROSS-REPO ASSUMPTION STATED HONESTLY: both legs were read AT SOURCE; NEITHER was verified against a live deployment - the ledger records the current mainnet wiring as repointed and the pot as empty. That is the arming condition, not an assumption.

PoC NOTE: poc-M02 uses the REAL NudgeRatchet; claim-2 P&L is 0.000000 (full cost recovered, protocol retains 0). `M02MintLeg` is a DISCLOSED TRANSCRIPTION of _executeMint - the real NFTMinterV2 needs solc ^0.8.24 and this repo pins 0.8.20. SAFE CONFIG: never set dispatcherIndex to an index whose dispatcher forwards to this contract; or make the payout value-aware; or take a haircut.
